methods.description: Rewrite related fractions with the same denominator, then compare or order their numerators. Use a supplied subdivision when the original denominators do not all divide into the largest one.
Use equal subdivisions from zero to one to place fractions, read their left-to-right order, and find division points strictly between given endpoints.

substantiveCorrections: Corrected the Theory fact: sharing a common multiple alone does not distinguish related denominators. The source definition is that one denominator is a multiple of another.

Qualified the common-denominator step to use a related largest denominator or one supplied by the task; qualified number-line placement to tasks that ask for it. D2 now explicitly supplies twelfths, retaining the original fractions, answer and working without teaching general LCM discovery.
Completed F2’s requested number-line check with exact eighth-division positions, and D5’s requested number-line placement with exact twelfth-division positions and a native plot.

Added three useful worked examples: a pair comparison, a full order with number-line placement, and all fractions strictly inside a supplied subdivision interval. No assessment was removed; all22 assessment values/IDs/options/answers and every quiz byte are preserved.
